reason: Transfer/leakage lens. (1) The node-count multiplier is NOT the problem: on all 135 confirmation videos the cap-4 insertion changes the predicted node count by exactly 0. (2) The precision estimate the idea relies on is not embryo-held-out. DaughterNet 'OOF' p comes from 5 folds by 44b6 leak group. Every held-out video was scored by a model trained on other videos of the SAME embryo; no fold held out a whole embryo, which is what private is. On top of that, the candidate pool depends on the in-sample detector: 62/151 GT parents are exact-frame candidates, and divisions need ~3 um accuracy. The steal gate (edge_prob <= 0.3) and the daughter-edge choices use the in-sample edge net. So even the measured precision is an upper bound for unseen embryos. (3) Measured transfer of this exact stage: SELECTION +0.0058 -> CONFIRMATION +0.0019 (33% retained; TP 16->20, FP 28->39, 90% CI [-0.0007, +0.0050]) -> public LB +0.001. The LB delta between two 3-decimal scores is +-0.001, so it is consistent with 0. The edge side of the insertion is already net-negative in-sample: +5 TP / +7 FP from steals and second-daughter edges. (4) The margin the idea wants to add has negative in-sample evidence. On SELECTION, cap 4 -> 6 added 50 insertions for 0 TP / +2 FP evaluable (-0.00034). Precision falls with rank, and in-sample marginal precision would fall further out of sample. (5) The 44b6 half of the per-embryo gate rests on one event. The whole 44b6 confirmation gain (+0.0015) is ONE TP on ONE video (44b6_d754aa59, video score +0.126), against 3 FP on 3 other videos. 44b6 crops are overlapping views of one recording, so '>= 0.17 on both embryos' cannot be estimated (n ~ 1-4 evaluable forks). (6) The density-scaled cap is refuted by data: Spearman(GT divisions, nodes) = 0.02 over 199 videos. It would add forks in dense regions, where they are unannotated and useless on train but can become FP on a denser private annotation. (7) The private-J argument is not a transfer argument in the idea's favour. With 15-50 GT divisions in the public embryo, sampling noise cannot explain J_pub 0.36 (P(J >= 0.32 | 20 GT) ~ 0.004). The private J is unknown (mixture break-even ~0.20), and the in-sample marginal p beyond cap 4 (0/2) is below every scenario's break-even. (8) The refined fallback is not new: the shipped exp48 ensemble threshold 0.4 was calibrated to equal OOF 0.5. So 's_c4_t0.5' IS the shipped config, and 'threshold minus 0.1' would be OOF 0.4, which is untested and has the same in-sample-pool problem. Net: any local gain from raising the cap would come from the in-sample pool and edge net plus noise-fitting on ~10 evaluable forks, not from a real private improvement.
fix_if_any: Do not raise the cap and do not scale it by track count; keep the shipped cap 4 / ensemble threshold 0.4. To make ANY division-aggressiveness decision transfer-safe: (a) retrain DaughterNet v1 with 2 folds BY EMBRYO (train 6bba -> score 44b6 and the reverse; ~20 min on a Kaggle T4, the recipe already exists). Re-run cap 4/6/8 in the lab with that p to measure how much pool precision drops when the embryo is truly unseen. Adopt a higher cap only if the embryo-held-out marginal precision is >= 0.25 with >= 8 marginal evaluable forks AND the insertion's edge-side delta (steals and second-daughter edges) is >= 0. (b) Count 44b6 events once per unique GT division id, not once per crop, before any 44b6 per-embryo test. (c) Spend the second-final division budget on J-invariant fork REMOVAL (e.g. the fork-midpoint >= 4 um rule, 11 FP / 0 TP), which helps under every private J and does not depend on in-sample positive precision.
realistic_public_gain: 0 (range -0.0005..+0.0002); private also ~0 (range -0.0005..+0.0005, sign-uncertain). The claimed +0.001..+0.002 private needs marginal out-of-sample precision ~0.25 beyond cap 4, while the in-sample marginal is 0/2.
